name: British Legion (with attached regulars at Cowpens)
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cowpens : "Nearly half of his men, 481 out of 1,158, were Loyalists." (his force at Cowpens, Jan 1781; Waxhaws May 1780 was 149 mounted per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banastre_Tarleton).

rows.label: Basking Ridge (captures Gen. Charles Lee)
rows.quote: Tarleton surrounded a house in Basking Ridge

rows.label: Monck's Corner (surprises Huger)
rows.quote: On the evening of 13 April, Tarleton intercepted a letter
rows.note: Battle fought 3 am on 14 April per the same article; Tarleton commanded the British Legion in the attack.

rows.label: Lenud's Ferry (scatters White's cavalry)
rows.quote: again scattered by Tarleton at Lenud's Ferry on 6 May

rows.label: Camden (starts pursuit of Buford)
rows.quote: Tarleton reached Camden late on May 28
rows.note: Commanded a detachment of about 270 men and a 3-pounder sent by Cornwallis on May 27.

rows.label: Waxhaws (defeats Buford)
rows.quote: On 29 May 1780, Colonel Tarleton, with a force of 149 mounted soldiers

rows.label: Battle of Camden (Legion cavalry pursuit)
rows.quote: Tarleton's cavalry delivered the coup de grace
rows.note: Article describes his cavalry/Legion; Tarleton led the Legion in the pursuit and is quoted on the battle. Battle date from events.json and Battle of Camden article.

rows.label: Fishing Creek (surprises Sumter)
rows.quote: British forces under Banastre Tarleton surprised the militia company
rows.note: Left the main army Aug 17 and crossed the Catawba the next morning with about 350 men.

rows.label: Blackstock's Farm (repulsed by Sumter)
rows.quote: Tarleton personally dismounted and carried the badly wounded Major Money
rows.note: Battle date November 20, 1780 from the same article.

rows.label: Battle of Cowpens (defeated by Morgan)
rows.quote: At 2:00 a.m. on January 17 Tarleton roused his troops

rows.label: Cowan's Ford area (Torrence's Tavern skirmish)
rows.quote: successful in a skirmish at Torrence's Tavern
rows.note: Date given in the parenthetical 'Cowan's Ford Skirmish, 1 February 1781'. The skirmish at Torrence's Tavern was a separate action from the main crossing; Tarleton is placed in the area, not at the ford itself. Corrected after independent check: Source places Tarleton at Torrence Tavern, not at the ford itself.

rows.label: Battle of Guilford Court House (wounded)
rows.quote: took part in the Battle of Guilford Courthouse in March 1781
rows.note: Day 15 March from events.json and the Battle of Guilford Court House article; the Tarleton article gives only the month and says he lost two fingers there.

rows.label: Charlottesville raid (to capture Jefferson and Assembly)
rows.quote: Around dawn, Tarleton reached the plantations of Castle Hill
rows.note: Article says Tarleton left Cornwallis's camp June 3 and arrived around dawn; June 4 date from the Charlottesville, Virginia article (Jouett's warning on June 4, 1781). Castle Hill is near Charlottesville.

rows.label: Gloucester Point (skirmish with Lauzun's Legion)
rows.quote: skirmished at Gloucester Point. Tarleton was unhorsed
rows.note: Cornwallis instructed him to hold Gloucester Point during the siege of Yorktown. Corrected after independent check: NPS Yorktown timeline: Oct 3 allied forces defeat Tarleton at Gloucester.

rows.label: Gloucester Point (garrison surrenders)
rows.quote: The British surrendered Gloucester Point to the French and Americans
rows.note: Date 19 October from the Siege of Yorktown article (troops at Gloucester also surrendered). Tarleton article says he held Gloucester Point; no source places him there by name on this exact day.
